recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit. If FM wants optional, coded, or repeating class values, handle that through the later R6 issue family such as FHIR-54234 rather than reopening FHIR-24641 implicitly.
issue_request: FHIR-24641 was a Published/Persuasive FM change request asking Coverage.class to carry assigning authority information for class numbers by changing the class value/number from a string-like value to Identifier. The resolution text is internally inconsistent about type/value and 1..* cardinality, but its accepted structure retained Coverage.class.type as CodeableConcept and changed the class value to Identifier.
initial_application: No commit or PR explicitly mentioning FHIR-24641 was found. The effective R5 application appears in broad commits 378239e087e8bfc9ed361cb19e0dcbbbeb4a07bc and 720258c80a99566e1259c4c1a1dcacd8fbc5abbf, which changed Coverage.class.value from string to Identifier, updated Coverage examples to nested Identifier syntax, and changed the class-value search parameter from string to token.
additional_context: Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source, R5 published output, and build.fhir.org all show Coverage.class as 0..*, Coverage.class.type as 1..1 CodeableConcept, Coverage.class.value as 1..1 Identifier, and Coverage.class.name as 0..1 string. Later FHIR-54234 is only Resolved - change required in this default run and treats the current 1..1 Identifier as the baseline for future R6 changes, so it does not justify changing cardinality for FHIR-24641 now.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative source, examples, and search parameter already convey Identifier semantics for Coverage.class.value; changing max to * based only on inconsistent resolution wording would be a new specification decision.
